clue.text: Cry about foot throughout the whole game

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the cry wraps around the foot

parts.note: to sob is to cry
the whole of something is all of it

explanation.surface: Someone yells about a foot injury from first whistle to last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throughout' is only a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Softball is a bat-and-ball sport, a close relative of baseball, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: About to enter craft after another citizen

indicators.note: after means the second craft comes behind the first one in the answer

parts.note: another craft, here a submarine, shortened to sub

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so the abbreviation for about sits within the craft

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft
C (circa) is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Someone is about to board a vessel following a fellow national.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after another' places SUB, a second craft, ahead of JECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject is a person owing allegiance to a state or monarch, a synonym for a citizen.

clue.text: Warnings about monarch being taken in by US soldier's deceits

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the warnings go round the rest

parts.note: golfers shout fore as a warning, so warnings are fores

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the monarch sits within the soldier

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A tale of royal warnings and an American soldier's trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgeries are fakes passed off as genuine, so they are deceits or frauds.

clue.text: Beginning to break, beams making harsh sounds

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken from break

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Dawn light breaks through as something creaks and groans.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's bray is a loud, grating call, so brays are harsh noises.

clue.text: Durability of novelty gift not half bad

indicators.note: bad means going wrong, signalling these letters are rearranged
not half keeps only the front half of the word gift

explanation.surface: A gimmicky present that turns out reasonably long-lasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' leaves GI from 'gift'; 'bad' scrambles NOVELTY plus GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Longevity is long life or lasting power, which is the same idea as durability.

clue.text: Head of bakery poked in bread before turning out

indicators.note: turning means the assembled letters are read backwards
poked in means pushed inside, so the letter enters the money

parts.note: bread and moola are both slang for money

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A baker's head pokes into the bread before it is turned out of the tin.
explanation.walkthrough: MOOLA with B inside is MOOLBA, and 'turning' reverses that. 'Bread' looks like a loaf but means money.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers that are out have opened, which is what being in full bloom means.

clue.text: Author's difficulty to write up basic intro to story

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing up means setting the word bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: rub is a difficulty, as in Hamlet's there's the rub
rough means basic or crude

indicators.note: the intro to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A writer struggles to draft a crude opening to a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' is 'is', a link. William S. Burroughs and Edgar Rice Burroughs were both writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Burroughs is the surname of famous novelists, so it names an example of a writer.

clue.text: Start rewriting notes

indicators.note: rewriting the word notes means putting its letters down in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin redrafting one's notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the beginning of something, as in the onset of winter, so a synonym for start.

clue.text: Guy embracing paramour, leaving old spa town

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the man wraps round the lover

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter for old is removed

parts.note: a paramour is a lover

explanation.surface: A man clasps his lover and leaves an old resort town.
explanation.walkthrough: MALVERN is a Worcestershire town in England, famous for its spring water.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Malvern grew as a Victorian water-cure resort, so it is an example of a spa resort.

clue.text: Release last bit of venom as some snakes do

definitions.text: Release last bit of venom as some snakes do

parts.words: Release last bit of venom as some snakes do
parts.note: certain cobras eject venom from the mouth at a target, and the whole clue describes that forceful expulsion

explanation.surface: A snake ejects the final drops of its poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last bit of' tempts a solver to take a final letter, but there is no wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain cobras project venom from the mouth at their enemies, and the verb for that forceful ejection is the same one people use for saliva.

clue.text: Steal pub's profit

parts.note: a bar is a pub; the 's is just a link
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: An accusation that a pub's takings were stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steal' looks like a verb but is the noun, as in 'it's a steal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something is a steal when it sells for much less than it is worth, a colloquial sense of a good buy.

clue.text: Study reviewed Spaniard's article on SA country

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: Peru is a country in South America

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed, looking at the article backwards

parts.note: las is the Spanish plural word for the

explanation.surface: Someone reviews an article by a Spaniard about a South American country.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination of something, so it is a study.

clue.text: This farm animal would be seen in vid

definitions.text: This farm animal would be seen in vid

parts.words: This farm animal would be seen in vid
parts.note: placing the female sheep inside the letters V I D forms a word meaning seen, so the clue describes that construction

explanation.surface: A sheep appears in a video clip.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the sheep inside VID spells VIEWED, which is what 'seen' means.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is the farm animal whose name, placed inside vid, produces a synonym of seen.

clue.text: This contains smell from audibly discharged guts

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so a word sounding like the synonym is taken

parts.note: sent means discharged or dispatched
bottle is British slang for courage, or guts

explanation.surface: Noisy intestines expelling something smelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent bottle is a small vessel holding perfume, so it holds a smell.

clue.text: Old fragment obtained by tiler when working is a fossil

indicators.note: obtained by means held by, so the scrambled tiler surrounds the rest
working means being reworked, signalling an anagram of tiler

parts.note: a bit is a fragment

explanation.surface: A tiler at work turns up an old piece, which proves to be a fossil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when working' rearranges TILER to TRILE, which goes round OBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilobites are extinct marine arthropods known only from their fossil remains, so one is an example of a fossil.

clue.text: UV problematic with tailor's tops

indicators.note: problematic suggests things gone awry, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Ultraviolet light causes trouble for a tailor's shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops' looks like clothing but is a verb meaning beats.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrival someone is to beat them in competition, so it means to top them.

clue.text: Fortification of body with exercise

parts.note: the Earth is a heavenly body
work can mean exercise, as in a workout

explanation.surface: Strengthening the body through physical training.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthwork is a bank of soil built as a defence, which is a kind of fortification.

clue.text: No particular interest about African country

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: not my bag means not my interest, so no bag is no particular interest

explanation.surface: Someone shows little enthusiasm for an African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a country on the west coast of Central Africa.

clue.text: Rain a bit? It's torrential around northern Roman province

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the letter for northern
torrential suggests wild turbulence, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A light drizzle turns into a downpour in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link. The drizzle sits in the surface, but the Romans' name for Britain is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia was the Latin name for the Roman-ruled part of Great Britain, a province of the empire.

clue.text: Dog with no head strength

indicators.note: with no head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a basset is a short-legged breed of hound

explanation.surface: A dog without a head would hardly show much strength.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a strong point or advantage, so it can mean a strength.

clue.text: Clobber engineers in outrage

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the engineers go into the outrage

parts.note: to appal is to outrage or shock
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers lash out in fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' is not hitting but British slang for clothes and gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is British slang for clothing, and apparel is a formal word for clothes.

clue.text: Centre of York being replaced with strangely drastic measure

indicators.note: being replaced with means these middle letters are swapped for the others
the centre of York is its two middle letters, picked for replacement
strangely means oddly arranged, so the letters of drastic are scrambled

explanation.surface: A city's centre gets a drastic redevelopment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges DRASTIC to ARDSTIC, which takes the place of OR in YORK.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard used for comparison, a figurative measure.

clue.text: Gap to help us enter part of harbour undamaged, we're informed

indicators.note: being informed means being told aloud, signalling that what is heard counts

parts.note: a quay is a landing place forming part of a harbour; whole means intact or undamaged

explanation.surface: A gap in the sea wall lets us into the harbour unharmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyhole is the opening for a key, the gap that lets us unlock a door and get in.

clue.text: Derision from one leaving GAP — shirt not ironed out

indicators.note: ironed out suggests smoothing and reshaping, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A departing customer mocks the clothes store Gap for an unpressed shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: GAP is a clothing retailer, which fits the shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A parting shot is a cutting remark made as someone departs, a final jibe.

clue.text: Bank holding money overturned transfer

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means flipped, read bottom to top
holding means containing, so the bank wraps round the money

parts.note: a tier is a bank or row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A bank keeping hold of cash reverses a transfer.
explanation.walkthrough: TIER with M inside is TIMER, and 'overturned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send money or refer a matter elsewhere, which is to transfer it.

clue.text: Agree, without borders, yard is dull

indicators.note: without borders means losing the outer letters of agree

explanation.surface: Boundary-free agreement about a yard sounds tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey describes something drab or lacking colour and interest, so it is a synonym for dull.

clue.text: Plant starts to unfurl lavishly in raised bed

indicators.note: in means placed inside the reversed bed
in a down clue, raised means lifted up, read bottom to top

parts.note: pit is British slang for a bed

indicators.note: the starts of the two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Flowers open lavishly in a raised garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a bulb plant grown for its cup-shaped spring flowers.

clue.text: Answer back from teen and from tweeny, 'Whatever'

indicators.note: the back of each word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A teenager and a younger child both answer back with a sulky 'Whatever'.
explanation.definitionFit: Any, as in any old thing, expresses indifference to the choice, the sense of whatever.

clue.text: Send communication after sheep run wild

indicators.note: after means the communication comes behind the sheep

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
to page someone is to send them a message

explanation.surface: Someone sends a message after the sheep escape.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently and uncontrollably, which is running wild.

clue.text: Shakespearean character, 5, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the hero of As You Like It, who hangs love poems on trees
the answer to 5-across read as a phrase gives a surname, so this is the first name of the actor with that surname

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare role, with a cross-reference to another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 5-across read as A BLOOM points at the actor Orlando Bloom, one example of a Bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a Shakespeare hero and also the first name of actor Bloom, the clue's two references.

clue.text: Current eroded banks of Slav river

indicators.note: eroded banks means the outer letters of Slav are worn away

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England

explanation.surface: A current wears away the banks of a Slavic river.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest thing is the most recent or up-to-date one, which is what current means.

clue.text: Captain leading the way for aircraft

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the captain comes first

parts.note: skip is short for skipper, a captain
a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: A pilot leads the way for the planes.
explanation.definitionFit: A skiplane is a plane fitted with skis to land on snow, so it is a kind of aircraft.
